evidence.quote: let renewalRefusal (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : LendingError option =
let outcome = Loans.renew today loan.Copy library
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The renewability rule (overdue, then limit, then holds, in the order DEC-004 gives) is in one Tier 2 function, renewalRefusal. Loans.renew now calls it. The Tier 3 view calls it too, for the `loans` listing. renewAll in Tier 3 only calls Loans.renew for each loan and collects the results. Views.renewalReason only maps a Tier 2 error to display text. The CLI used to call Loans.renew directly and make the success and failure decision itself. It now goes through a use case and only formats the view, so a Tier 4 re-entry was removed.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect in Tier 1/2. The clock is read only through the existing Clock port. Saving goes through the existing `commit` helper and the Store port. The old CLI `renew` branch called ports.Store.Load/Save and Loans.renew directly. That branch is now a Tier 3 use case, which moves the logic away from Tier 4. `renew-all` is a single commit, so its decision and its saving are not interleaved.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The limit is defined once, as Policy.renewLimit. The refusal and the "renewal n of m" display both read it. The "renewed N of N times" reason takes its number from the error value, which Tier 2 produces. The refusal order is written once, in renewalRefusal, and `renew`, `loans` and `renew-all` all use it. No fact is copied.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-member-type limit is a Tier 2 policy value, and finding the borrower's limit is a Tier 2 function (renewLimitOf). The enforcement in renewalRefusal uses it. The Tier 3 views only call renewLimitOf to show the limit. No member-type branching was added in Tier 3 or Tier 4.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No production change adds an effect. Policy.renewLimit and renewLimitOf are pure functions. The Tier 3 views get the library passed in and do not read anything from the outside. The existing ports and commit flow are unchanged.

evidence.quote: elif loan.Renewals >= renewLimitOf loan library then Some(RenewLimitReached(copyId, renewLimitOf loan library))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Policy.renewLimit holds the limits 2, 1 and 4 and nothing else defines them. renewLimitOf is the one way to look up the borrower's limit. Both the enforcement and the display use it, so the "of N" on the success line, the `loans` reason and the refusal agree. It is called twice in one line of renewalRefusal, which is untidy but not a duplicated fact. DEC-004 is updated to revision 2 in the same change, so the document and the code stay in step. The fallback to Standard when the member is missing is a single Tier 2 default.
